findings.title: Referer host check is the only access control and is trivially spoofable
findings.body: ensure_embeddable trusts request.referer to decide whether the embed endpoint may be served, and then sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL. Referer headers are client-controlled and can be stripped or forged by non-browser clients, so any caller can fetch the embed page. Combined with ALLOWALL, the page can be framed from any origin. The check gates only on referer, not on a shared secret or origin validation.

findings.title: Anonymous requests enqueue retrieve jobs without throttle bypass and can trigger remote fetches
findings.body: Every request to best without an existing TopicEmbed enqueues a retrieve_topic job with an arbitrary embed_url. TopicRetriever only throttles per URL via redis setnx, so an attacker can enumerate many distinct URLs on the embeddable host to cause unbounded remote HTTP fetches and job queue growth.

findings.title: Port handling in absolutize_urls is wrong for non-default ports and scheme
findings.body: prefix appends the port unless it is 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, and uri.port for an https URL on port 80 or http on 443 is wrongly dropped/kept. More importantly the prefix is built with string << on a fresh string each call, which is fine, but the scheme check is missing: URLs with other schemes are not constrained here. The main consequence is incorrect absolute links for some URL/port combinations.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string and interpolates unescaped title/url into HTML
findings.body: contents << ... modifies the string passed in by the caller (PollFeed passes i.content which is then reused), and the url is interpolated unescaped into an href inside HTML that is stored as raw_html and rendered without cooking, creating a stored XSS vector if the URL contains quotes. Since cook_method raw_html skips sanitization, feed content is stored and displayed verbatim.

findings.title: Raw HTML from remote feeds/pages is stored with raw_html cook method, skipping sanitization
findings.body: Post.cook returns raw when cook_method is raw_html, so remote content (RSS items or fetched pages via Readability, which is only partially whitelisted and not applied to feed content) is rendered unsanitized into the forum and served to readers, enabling stored XSS from any imported feed.

findings.title: i.content may be nil and scrub is called on it
findings.body: SimpleRSS items without a content element return nil for i.content, so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll loop, skipping all remaining feed items.

findings.title: open() of a URL uses Kernel#open which can execute commands or read local files
findings.body: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with a string relies on Kernel#open, which in older Ruby interprets pipe-prefixed strings as shell commands and otherwise reads local files. Use URI.open/open-uri explicitly or a safer fetch.

findings.title: embeddable_host comparison is case sensitive and ignores port
findings.body: invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI(...).host exactly, so a host with different case (Eviltrout.com) is rejected, and the controller's referer check does the same. Inconsistent with browser host semantics and may reject valid embeds.

findings.title: Disqus import now fetches each thread's remote page and discards the post's per-comment creation
findings.body: The import replaces PostCreator creation of a permalink post with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches the live page over HTTP. Dry-run and offline imports now depend on network access, and the blank line left behind plus the removed category option break the documented CLI interface (the -c option is removed without replacement).

findings.title: cook_method check returns raw content without any escaping for all raw_html posts
findings.body: cook short-circuits to return raw for raw_html posts, bypassing Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hooks and any sanitization. Combined with cook being called in before_create_tasks, posts created this way are never filtered by plugins.

findings.title: skip_validations now changes save behaviour for all revisions, and return value is ignored
findings.body: update_post calls @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) and ignores the result. Previously the same save ran, but with validations skipped on imported posts, rate-limit and spam validations bypass is now possible; the failed save is also silently ignored, so revise! returns true even when the post failed to save.

findings.title: force: true on create_table will drop existing top_topics data on migration
findings.body: Adding force: true makes the migration drop and recreate the top_topics table if it already exists, destroying any existing rows. Migrations that have already run are unaffected, but on a DB where the table exists this silently wipes data.

findings.title: Adding NOT NULL column with default to large posts table rewrites the table
findings.body: add_column with default and null: false on Postgres of older versions rewrites the whole posts table under an exclusive lock, which can block a production forum for a long time.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated into a JavaScript string literal
findings.body: The referer is inserted into a script string without JavaScript escaping. A referer containing a quote or newline breaks out of the string and injects script. Use json or escape_javascript and validate the origin.

findings.title: Success assertions placed in after hook and error tests use weak checks
findings.body: The response assertions are in an after block, so they run after each example rather than as part of it, and the tests are not checking the rendered behaviour for the loading case. Failures are reported confusingly and the 404 test does not verify the status.

findings.title: Spec does not cover the update path's content_sha1 handling or the no-change case
findings.body: The 'Supports updating the post' test does not assert the embed record's content_sha1 was updated nor that unchanged content skips revision, so regressions in the update logic would pass.
